facts.body: When the English Base Set launched in January 1999, the artwork window sat flat against the yellow border — no shadow. A short way into the print run, Wizards of the Coast added a thin grey shadow down the right side and along the bottom of that window. Every card printed before that change lacks it; every card after has it. Collectors named the earlier ones "Shadowless" long afterward.
facts.why_it_matters: So you can sort a pile of Base Set cards in seconds: look at the right edge of the picture box. A clean edge means it came from those first few weeks, and those copies sell for meaningfully more than the ones printed for the two years that followed.

facts.hook: Base Set is the only main English expansion with no set symbol.
facts.body: Every other English main-series set stamps a symbol beside the artwork. Base Set doesn't — so the fastest identification test is the absence of one, plus a card number out of 102.
facts.why_it_matters: So if you're digging through a bulk pile and a card has no little symbol beside the artwork and says something out of 102, you're holding a 1999 Base Set card — no card names required.
sources: Big Orbit Cards: Base Set identification guide

facts.hook: Base Set is 102 cards: 69 Pokémon, 26 Trainers, 7 Energy.
facts.body: The 16 holo rares are cards 1 through 16 — Charizard sits at 4/102. The set also established the layout the TCG still uses today: yellow border, HP top-right, and the weakness / resistance / retreat row along the bottom.
facts.why_it_matters: So the most famous card in the hobby, Charizard, sits at 4/102 purely because holo rares came first and C comes early in the alphabet. The hobby's landmark number is an accident of sorting.
sources: Bill's Archive: Base Set complete guide

facts.hook: There are two Pikachus in Base Set, and one is worth more.
facts.body: Pikachu 58/102 exists with red cheeks and with yellow cheeks. Red Cheeks appears only in the 1st Edition and Shadowless printings — every Unlimited Pikachu is Yellow Cheeks. Both PSA and CGC label the variant on the slab.
facts.why_it_matters: So if you own a Base Set Pikachu, check the cheeks. Red means it came from the earliest printings — worth more than the yellow-cheeked version everyone else has.
sources: Fanatics Collect: 1999 Base Set lot description (variant confirmed)

facts.hook: Nobody actually knows how many 1st Edition Base Set cards were printed.
facts.body: The figure repeated everywhere is 10,000 copies of each card. It has never been confirmed by Wizards of the Coast or The Pokémon Company. It circulates as community lore, not documented fact.
facts.why_it_matters: So the next time someone quotes a print-run number at you as though it settles an argument, remember that the most repeated figure in the hobby has no source behind it.
sources: Fanatics Collect auction description (states the figure has never been confirmed)
facts.note: Published as an unconfirmed-claim story, never as a print-run figure. Single-source; framed accordingly.
